findings.title: Postgres call inside a loop in queueService.claimNextJob
findings.consequence: The loop makes a round trip (UPDATE jobs) on every pass until it finds what it wants and returns. Usually that is one or two trips, but when nothing matches it makes one trip per item, every time.
findings.fix: Do it in one query: WHERE id IN (...), a bulk insert/upsert (createMany, insertMany), or load the rows once before the loop.

findings.title: SELECT jobs scans all of jobs on every request
findings.consequence: Counting or summing with no WHERE reads every row of jobs each time. It is quick today and grows linearly with the table, and every caller pays it.
findings.fix: Keep running counters (update them when rows change), cache the result for a few seconds, or restrict the query with a WHERE on an indexed column.

findings.title: Every open tab polls GET /stats every 5 s
findings.consequence: The browser asks whether anything changed even when nothing did. 10,000 open tabs make about 2,000 requests per second to GET /stats, almost all returning the same data. Cost grows with users, not with how often data changes.
findings.fix: Push changes instead (Server-Sent Events or WebSocket), poll less often, or use long polling.

findings.title: Each pushed message makes every browser call GET /stats
findings.consequence: The server pushes an event and every connected page answers by requesting GET /stats. 100 open dashboards and 20 events per second become 2,000 requests per second to GET /stats, which is more load than polling would cause.
findings.fix: Send the data the page needs inside the pushed message, or debounce the refresh.

findings.title: Redis call inside a loop in queueService.claimNextJob
findings.consequence: The loop makes a round trip (ZRANGEBYSCORE queue:priority:{}) on every pass until it finds what it wants and returns. Usually that is one or two trips, but when nothing matches it makes one trip per item, every time.
findings.fix: Fetch everything in one command (MGET, a pipeline, or one sorted-set query) instead of one per item.

findings.title: Page polls even though it already has a live WebSocket
findings.consequence: Updates already arrive over the socket, so the timer mostly repeats work and adds steady load.
findings.fix: Poll only while the socket is disconnected, or drop the timer.

findings.title: idx_jobs_status duplicates idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at on jobs
findings.consequence: idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at already gives the database an index starting with the same columns, so idx_jobs_status is never needed for reads. Every insert and update still has to maintain both, which costs write time and disk.

findings.title: Worker checks for work every 1 s even when there is none
findings.consequence: Each idle worker keeps querying the store. With 20 workers that is a steady stream of empty reads, and new jobs wait up to 1 s before anyone notices them.
findings.fix: Block on the queue instead of polling (BRPOP / BLMOVE, BullMQ, or LISTEN/NOTIFY in Postgres).
